rules.title: State minimum wage $16.90/hour (2026)
rules.plain_english: Every California employer, no matter how small, must pay at least $16.90 per hour for all hours worked starting January 1, 2026. A higher city or county rate overrides this where the work is done.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Every employer, regardless of the number of employees, shall pay to each employee wages not less than the following: (1) Sixteen dollars and ninety cents ($16.90) per hour for all hours worked, effective January 1, 2026;
rules.notes: Exempt from minimum wage per DLSE FAQ: outside salespersons; parent, spouse or child of the employer; apprentices regularly indentured under the Division of Apprenticeship Standards. Separate higher state rates exist for fast food and health care (not normally construction). Public works projects require prevailing wage instead (separate domain).

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §4(A); MW-2026 https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf; DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_minimumwage.htm

rules.title: Higher city/county minimum wage must be paid
rules.plain_english: If the city or county where the employee works has a higher minimum wage than the state, the employer must pay the higher local rate. Many California cities are higher than $16.90.

parameters.local_rate_list_referenced_by_DLSE: UC Berkeley Labor Center inventory of city and county minimum wages (not an official DIR table)

rules.applies_to: Employers with employees working within a city or county that has its own minimum wage ordinance
rules.citation: Labor Code 1182.12; local ordinances (DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ Q3)
rules.verbatim_quote: if a local entity (city or county) has adopted a higher minimum wage, employees must be paid the local wage where it is higher than the state or federal minimum wage rates.
rules.notes: No local rates were read from official city sources in this pass; a tool must look up the jobsite city/county rate (many adjust each July 1 or January 1). For construction crews moving between jobsites, the rate applies per location where hours are worked (verify each ordinance's coverage threshold, e.g., minimum hours worked in the city).

verification.checked_against: DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_minimumwage.htm (Q3, "stricter standard" paragraph)

rules.title: State minimum wage adjusts each year by CPI-W (max 3.5%)
rules.plain_english: The state minimum wage now changes every January 1 based on inflation. It can go up by at most 3.5% in a year and can never go down.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: After the state minimum wage reached $15 an hour, the rate is adjusted annually for inflation based on the national consumer price index for urban wage earners and clerical workers (CPI-W). However, the minimum wage cannot be lowered, even if there is a negative CPI, and the highest raise allowed in any one year is 3.5 percent.
rules.notes: A tool should store rates by effective date and refresh each year from MW-20XX orders published by DIR.

rules.title: Minimum wage applies to all hours in each payroll period, including piece rate
rules.plain_english: For every pay period, total pay must equal at least minimum wage times all hours worked, whether the worker is paid hourly, by the piece (e.g., per square or linear foot) or by commission.
rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: Every employer shall pay to each employee, on the established payday for the period involved, not less than the applicable minimum wage for all hours worked in the payroll period, whether the remuneration is measured by time, piece, commission, or otherwise.
rules.notes: Piece-rate workers also have separate rest/recovery and nonproductive time pay rules (Labor Code 226.2) that were not read in this pass.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §4(B)

rules.title: Learner rate: 85% of minimum wage for first 160 hours
rules.plain_english: Under the IWC wage orders that have a learner clause (for example Order 4, which covers office staff), a new worker with no similar experience may be paid 85% of the minimum wage, rounded to the nearest nickel, for their first 160 hours only. Wage Order 16, which covers on-site construction workers, has no learner rate, so field employees must get the full minimum wage from day one.

parameters.source_orders: IWC Orders 1-15 §4(A) (verified in Order 4-2001); absent from Order 16-2001 and MW-2026

rules.applies_to: New employees with no previous similar or related experience who are covered by an IWC order that contains a learner clause (Orders 1-15, e.g., Order 4 office/clerical staff of a contractor). NOT available for on-site construction, drilling, logging or mining employees covered by IWC Order 16-2001.
rules.citation: IWC Orders 1-15 §4(A) learner clause (e.g., IWC Order 4-2001 §4(A)); DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ Q4. Not in IWC Order 16-2001 §4 or MW-2026.
rules.verbatim_quote: There is an exception for learners, regardless of age, who may be paid not less than 85 percent of the minimum wage rounded to the nearest nickel during their first 160 hours of employment in occupations in which they have no previous similar or related experience.
rules.notes: Derived rate: 16.90 x 0.85 = 14.365, rounded to nearest nickel = $14.35. Local ordinances may not allow a learner rate; check locally. Verification: WO16 §4(A)-(B) and MW-2026 have no learner clause; Order 4-2001 §4(A) does.

verification.checked_against: DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_minimumwage.htm (Q4); IWC Order 4-2001 https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle4.pdf §4(A) "LEARNERS" clause; IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §4 (no learner clause); MW-2026 https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf (no learner clause)
verification.correction: The learner subminimum is in the industry wage orders that contain a learner clause (e.g., IWC Order 4 §4(A)), not in MW-2026. IWC Order 16-2001, which covers on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining, has no learner clause in §4. A construction tool must not apply the 85% rate to WO16 field employees. Corrected the citation, source_location, applies_to and plain_english, and added not_available_under_wage_order_16. The 85%, 160-hour and nearest-nickel figures and the $14.35 derivation are confirmed.

rules.title: Exempt (EAP) salary must be at least 2x minimum wage ($70,304/yr in 2026)
rules.plain_english: To treat a manager, administrator or professional as exempt from overtime and meal/rest rules, they must mainly (over half their time) do exempt duties and earn a salary of at least twice the state minimum wage for 40 hours a week: $5,858.67/month or $70,304/year in 2026.

parameters.primarily_means: more than one-half of work time

rules.applies_to: Executive, administrative and professional employees of construction/drilling/logging/mining employers
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall be considered to be employed in an administrative, executive, or professional capacity unless the person is primarily engaged in the duties which meet the test of the exemption, and earns a monthly salary equivalent to not less than two (2) times the state minimum wage for full-time employment.
rules.notes: Dollar figures are computed from the primary rule and the $16.90 state rate (local minimum wages do not change the state exemption threshold). Duties test also required.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.2 §1(A), §1(A)(4) (full-time = 40 h/week), §2(O); dollar figures recomputed: 2 x 16.90 x 40 = 1,352/wk, x52 = 70,304/yr, /12 = 5,858.67/mo

rules.title: Employer provides tools unless worker earns 2x minimum wage
rules.plain_english: If tools or equipment are required or needed for the job, the employer must provide and maintain them. Only workers paid at least twice the minimum wage ($33.80/hour in 2026) can be required to bring their own customary hand tools.

parameters.rule: if hourly_rate < 2 * min_wage: employer must provide and maintain all required tools and equipment
parameters.uniforms: required uniforms provided and maintained by employer (WO16 §8(A))

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: When the employer requires the use of tools or equipment or they are necessary for the performance of a job, such tools and equipment shall be provided and maintained by the employer, except that an employee whose wages are at least two (2) times the minimum wage may provide and maintain hand tools and equipment customarily required by the particular trade or craft
rules.notes: Threshold computed from the $16.90 state minimum wage; whether a higher local minimum wage changes the 2x threshold was not verified. Labor Code 2802 expense reimbursement (vehicle, phone) still applies.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.6 §8(A)-(B)

rules.title: Maximum meal and lodging credits against minimum wage (2026)
rules.plain_english: An employer may count meals or lodging toward minimum wage only with a voluntary written agreement, and only up to set amounts (for 2026: breakfast $6.10, lunch $8.42, dinner $11.28; private room $79.46/week).

max_credits_2026_usd.apartment_rule: two-thirds of ordinary rental value, not more than max

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001) (e.g., remote jobsite camps)
rules.verbatim_quote: Meals or lodging may not be credited against the minimum wage without a voluntary written agreement between the employer and the employee.
rules.notes: Signing the 2810.5 Notice to Employee does not count as the voluntary written agreement (per DLSE template).

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.6 §9(C)-(E); MW-2026 https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf §3 (all eight 2026 amounts match)

rules.title: Overtime 1.5x after 8 hours/day, 40 hours/week, and first 8 hours of 7th day
rules.plain_english: Pay time-and-a-half for hours over 8 in a workday (up to 12), over 40 in a workweek, and for the first 8 hours on the seventh consecutive day worked in a workweek.

parameters.workday: any consecutive 24-hour period beginning at the same time each calendar day
parameters.workweek: any 7 consecutive days starting with the same calendar day each week (fixed 168 hours)
parameters.no_rate_combining: employer need not combine more than one overtime rate for the same hour (WO16 §3(D))
parameters.hours_counted: hours actually worked (paid sick/holiday hours not worked do not count)

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001); age 18+ and 16-17 year olds not required to attend school
rules.verbatim_quote: One and one-half times the employee's regular rate of pay for all hours worked in excess of eight hours up to and including 12 hours in any workday, and for the first eight hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek; and
rules.notes: Collective bargaining agreements meeting the 30%-above-minimum-wage test are exempt from WO16 §3(A)-(E) (see cba-hours-meal-exemption-30-percent). Public works have separate overtime rules (Labor Code 1810-1815).

verification.checked_against: DLSE Overtime FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_overtime.htm; IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.3 §3(A)(1)(a), §2(S)-(T), §3(D)

rules.title: Double time after 12 hours/day and after 8 hours on the 7th consecutive day
rules.plain_english: Pay double the regular rate for hours over 12 in a workday and for hours over 8 on the seventh consecutive day of work in the workweek.
rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: Double the employee's regular rate of pay for all hours worked in excess of 12 hours in any workday and for all hours worked in excess of eight on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek.

verification.checked_against: DLSE Overtime FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_overtime.htm; IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.3-4 §3(A)(1)(b)

rules.title: How to compute the regular rate for overtime
rules.plain_english: Overtime is paid on the 'regular rate', which includes hourly pay plus shift differentials, piece pay, commissions and non-discretionary bonuses. With two or more rates in a week, use a weighted average; for non-exempt salaried workers divide weekly salary by 40.

parameters.multiple_rates: regular_rate = total_week_earnings / total_week_hours (including OT hours); OT premium added on top
parameters.flat_sum_nondiscretionary_bonus: bonus / maximum legal regular hours in bonus period, then 1.5x or 2x for OT hours
parameters.production_bonus: bonus / total hours worked in period; add 0.5x (or 1x for double time) per OT hour
excluded: pay for non-working time (vacation, holiday, illness)
parameters.floor: regular rate may never be less than applicable minimum wage

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.citation: Labor Code 510; IWC Order 16-2001 §3(A)(1)(c); DLSE Overtime FAQ Q1, Q3, Q4
rules.verbatim_quote: If you are paid two or more rates by the same employer during the workweek, the regular rate is the "weighted average" which is determined by dividing your total earnings for the workweek, including earnings during overtime hours, by the total hours worked during the workweek, including the overtime hours.
rules.notes: Meal/rest premiums are paid at the 'regular rate of compensation' (Ferra v. Loews, 2021 - case law, not read here).

rules.title: Overtime may be paid on the next regular payday
rules.plain_english: Overtime earned in one pay period must be paid no later than the payday for the next regular pay period. Straight-time wages cannot be delayed.

parameters.deadline: payday of the next regular payroll period after the period in which OT was earned
parameters.wage_statement_correction: OT hours may be recorded as a correction on the next itemized statement with the dates corrected

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Overtime wages must be paid no later than the payday for the next regular payroll period following the payroll period in which the overtime wages were earned.

verification.checked_against: DLSE Paydays FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_paydays.htm (LC 204(b)(2) paragraph and Q2)

rules.title: All hours 'suffered or permitted' must be paid, even unauthorized overtime
rules.plain_english: If the employer knew or should have known the employee was working, the time must be paid, including overtime that was not approved. The employer may discipline for breaking the policy but must still pay. Overtime pay cannot be waived.

parameters.hours_worked_definition: time subject to employer control, including all time suffered or permitted to work (WO16 §2(J))

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.citation: Labor Code 1194; IWC Order 16-2001 §2(J); DLSE Overtime FAQ Q2, Q9
rules.verbatim_quote: California's wage and hour laws require that the employee be compensated for any hours he or she is "suffered or permitted to work, whether or not required to do so."
rules.notes: Relevant to timekeeping checks: pre-shift tailgate meetings, yard time and loading tools are typically hours worked when required by the employer.

rules.title: Alternative workweek: up to 10 regular hours/day in construction
rules.plain_english: With a properly adopted alternative workweek schedule, construction employees can work up to 10 hours a day (within 40 hours a week) without daily overtime. Hours beyond the schedule or over 40 still get 1.5x, and over 12 hours gets 2x.

parameters.ot_1_5x: hours beyond regularly scheduled AWS hours and over 40/week
parameters.ot_2x: over 12 hours/day and over 8 hours on days beyond the regularly scheduled workdays
parameters.public_works: AWS requiring >8 hours/day may not be used on public works in violation of Labor Code 1810-1815

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: The alternative workweek schedule shall provide for work by the affected employees of no longer than ten (10) hours per day within a 40 hour workweek without the payment to the affected employees of an overtime rate of compensation pursuant to this section.
rules.notes: Valid only if adopted by the election procedure in WO16 §3(C).

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.4 §3(B)(1)(a)-(i)

rules.title: Alternative workweek adoption and repeal election steps
rules.plain_english: To adopt an alternative workweek, the employer must propose it in writing, hold disclosure meetings at least 14 days before, win a secret ballot by two-thirds of the work unit, wait 30 days before requiring the new hours, and report the results to DIR within 30 days and post them at the jobsite.

parameters.approval_vote: at least 2/3 of affected employees in the work unit
parameters.ballot: secret ballot during regular hours at work site, before work is performed
parameters.report_to: DIR Office of the Director - Research, P.O. Box 420603, San Francisco, CA 94142-0603
parameters.work_unit: all nonexempt employees of one employer within a given craft who share a common work site

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: adopted in a secret ballot election, held before the performance of work, by at least a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the affected employees in the work unit.
rules.notes: Failure to make the written disclosure/meetings makes the election null and void. Do not send ballots to DIR; only results.

rules.title: No discipline for refusing more than 72 hours in a workweek
rules.plain_english: An employee cannot be fired or disciplined for refusing to work more than 72 hours in a workweek, except in a genuine emergency.

parameters.exception: emergency = unpredictable or unavoidable occurrence at unscheduled intervals requiring immediate action (WO16 §2(F))

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: No employee shall be terminated, disciplined or otherwise discriminated against for refusing to work more than 72 hours in any workweek, except in an emergency as defined in Section 2(F) above.

rules.title: Employee-requested makeup time: no daily OT up to 11 hours
rules.plain_english: If an employee asks in writing to make up time lost for a personal obligation in the same workweek, the makeup hours do not trigger daily overtime unless the day goes over 11 hours or the week over 40.
rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001) (also applies under CBA unless CBA says otherwise)
rules.verbatim_quote: the hours of that makeup work time, if performed in the same workweek in which the work time was lost, may not be counted toward computing the total number of hours worked in a day for purposes of the overtime requirements, except for hours in excess of 11 hours of work in one (1) day or forty (40) hours of work in one (1) workweek.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §3(F)

rules.title: One day's rest in seven (may accumulate in construction)
rules.plain_english: Employees are entitled to one day of rest in seven. In construction, rest days may be accumulated when the job reasonably requires 7+ straight days, but each calendar month must still include the equivalent of one day off in seven. Employees cannot be disciplined for refusing the 7th day.

parameters.accumulation_allowed: when nature of employment reasonably requires 7+ consecutive days

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.citation: Labor Code 551-552; IWC Order 16-2001 §3(G); DLSE Overtime FAQ Q6
rules.verbatim_quote: in each calendar month, the employee shall receive the equivalent of one (1) day’s rest in seven (7).
rules.notes: Seventh-consecutive-day overtime rates still apply.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §3(G); DLSE Overtime FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_overtime.htm (7th-day discipline answer)

rules.title: Union CBA exemption from overtime/meal rules requires pay 30% above minimum wage
rules.plain_english: Wage Order 16 overtime, alternative workweek and meal period sections do not apply to employees under a valid union agreement that sets wages, hours and conditions, pays premium rates for all overtime, and pays at least 30% more than the state minimum wage ($21.97/hour in 2026).

still_applies: §3(F) makeup time unless CBA says otherwise
§5 reporting time unless CBA says otherwise
requirements: valid CBA expressly providing wages, hours of work and working conditions
premium wage rates for all overtime hours

rules.applies_to: Union-represented construction employees
rules.verbatim_quote: if the agreement provides premium wage rates for all overtime hours worked and a regular hourly rate of pay for those employees of not less than thirty (30) percent more than the state minimum wage. (See Labor Code Section 514).

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.5 §3(H), p.5 §5(D), p.7 §10(E); 1.30 x 16.90 = 21.97 recomputed

rules.title: 30-minute meal period before end of 5th hour
rules.plain_english: An employee working more than 5 hours must get an uninterrupted, duty-free 30-minute meal period starting no later than the end of the 5th hour. It can be waived by mutual consent only if the whole day is 6 hours or less.

parameters.latest_start: end of 5th hour of work (before start of 6th hour)
parameters.required_to_stay_on_premises: then meal period must be paid

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: No employer shall employ any person for a work period of more than five (5) hours without a meal period of not less than thirty (30) minutes, except that when a work period of not more than six (6) hours will complete the day’s work the meal period may be waived by mutual consent of employer and employee.
rules.notes: Timing rule (end of 5th/10th hour) is from the DLSE Meal Periods FAQ citing Brinker (2012). Unpaid if fully relieved of duty.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.7 §10(A); DLSE Meal Periods FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_mealperiods.htm (Q3 timing per Brinker; on-premises meal must be paid)

rules.title: Second 30-minute meal period before end of 10th hour
rules.plain_english: An employee working more than 10 hours must get a second 30-minute meal period starting by the end of the 10th hour. It can be waived only if the day is 12 hours or less and the first meal was not waived.
rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: An employer may not employ an employee for a work period of more than ten (10) hours per day without providing the employee with a second meal period of not less than 30 minutes, except that if the total hours worked is no more than twelve (12) hours, the second meal period may be waived by mutual consent of employer and employee only if the first meal period was not waived.

verification.checked_against: IWC Order 16-2001 PDF https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (IWC Form 1114 Rev. 11/2025, re-fetched 2026-11-25) p.7 §10(B); DLSE Meal Periods FAQ https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_mealperiods.htm (Q3)

rules.title: On-duty (paid) meal period needs written, revocable agreement
rules.plain_english: A paid on-the-job meal period is allowed only if the nature of the work truly prevents relief from all duty and there is a written agreement that the employee can revoke in writing at any time.

parameters.test: objective: any employee in that job would be prevented from being relieved of all duty

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.citation: Labor Code 512; IWC Order 16-2001 §10(D); DLSE Meal Periods FAQ
rules.verbatim_quote: An “on duty” meal period shall be permitted only when the nature of the work prevents employee from being relieved of all duty and when, by written agreement between the parties, an on-the-job paid meal period is agreed to and complies with Labor Code Section 512.
rules.notes: The revocation-in-writing statement requirement is stated in the DLSE Meal Periods FAQ.

rules.title: Missed meal period: 1 extra hour of pay per workday
rules.plain_english: If a compliant meal period is not provided, the employer owes the employee one additional hour of pay at the regular rate of compensation for that workday.

parameters.unit: per workday the meal period is not provided

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.verbatim_quote: If an employer fails to provide an employee a meal period in accordance with the applicable provisions of this order, the employer shall pay the employee one (1) hour of pay at the employee’s regular rate of compensation for each workday that the meal period is not provided.
rules.notes: DLSE: premium is not hours worked for OT and has a 3-year limitations period (Murphy v. Kenneth Cole). DLSE late-payment FAQ: premiums are wages subject to Labor Code 210 (Naranjo 2022). Where a CBA has a final and binding dispute mechanism for meal periods, the CBA prevails.
